turns.prompt_text: it looks to be no rust on the bolts however I'm unable to get them loose
turns.response_html:
Since the bolts aren't rusted, they are likely seized due to over-tightening or thread-locking adhesive. Try these mechanical techniques to break them loose:

  • Shock the Threads: Place your wrench on the bolt and strike the handle sharply with a rubber mallet. This "shocks" the friction bond better than a steady pull.
  • Increase Leverage: Use a cheater bar (a hollow metal pipe) over your wrench handle to multiply your torque.
  • Tighten to Loosen: Try to tighten the bolt slightly first; this tiny movement can break the initial seal.
  • Apply Heat: Use a hair dryer or heat gun on the surrounding metal for several minutes to expand the nut or hole, making it larger than the bolt.
  • Hammer Tapping: Tap the head of the bolt directly with a hammer several times to disrupt any internal thread binding.
